<!-- pr-reviewer: d36f23819158458e61e03692cb5f3ece714c49df -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (a `feat`: merges at the next cut; the checkbox needs the maintainer's hand check).

**What looks good**
- Validation matches the project loader: `tool_library.rs:read_body` runs the same `ToolBodyDto::to_body` plus `tool_body::fits` that `project/validate.rs:155-156` runs, and the command re-checks `fits` (`tool_import.rs:117`) as `SetToolBody` does. A bad body refuses the whole file naming the tool, with nothing applied and no history entry (pinned by `a_malformed_or_ill_fitting_body_refuses_the_file_by_name`).
- Staleness: import only adds new tools (an existing name arrives as "Name (2)"), so no operation can reference an imported tool and none can hold a stale clear verdict. No existing tool's body is rewritten.
- Undo: `invert` removes exactly the added entities, body included; the old state comes back (`holders_off_lands_every_tool_bare_and_undo_restores`).
- Toggle off: every body is dropped before the skip/identity check, so tools land bare, and the report counts `holders_left_out`. With the toggle on, the skip compares record AND body through the saved DTO, so a re-import of an identical tool does not duplicate.
- Old `.camtools` files without `body` parse unchanged (`a_file_without_bodies_imports_as_before...`); the default `new()` is holders-on, a no-op without bodies.
- The preference is user-level (`prefs.rs`), written only when off and absent reads as on, so older prefs files load unchanged. MCP rejects a non-boolean `holders` by name. Script API shares the one `import_tools` path.
- Process: PROCESS_VERSION bumped to 17 for the skill edit, no CHANGELOG edit, no snapshot PNGs, decision file present, `Fixes #889`, `Changelog:`-style body complete. No unwrap/expect/panic or unchecked casts in the diff.

**Local results (merged with main; branch was already up to date with upstream/main, mergeable)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tool_library` | 13 passed |
| `tool_library_holders` | 5 passed |
| `view_prefs` | 7 passed |
| `mcp` | 13 passed |
| `project_roundtrip` | 71 passed |
| `camcraft-ui --lib` (from crates/ui) | 533 passed, 5 ignored |
| `clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

**Requested before merge**: none.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. PROCESS_VERSION 17 collides with other process PRs; renumber at merge, and add the #681 announcement comment.
2. A malformed body refuses the file even with "Import tool holders" unticked, because parsing validates before the toggle applies. This is the safer behaviour (a corrupt file is named), but a user who unticks to dodge a bad holder still gets the refusal.
3. No test pins "import does not touch an existing tool's operations"; it holds structurally today (add-only), so a future change to overwrite-on-import would need an explicit stale step.
4. The "Import tool holders" checkbox (`pages.rs:~995`) is covered by a structural UI test but needs the maintainer's hand check.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** (Full re-review at the high tier of the rework onto #899's ImportMode; author is mkinney, our own PR.)

**What looks good**
- #899 semantics intact: `new` / `with_mode` delegate to `with_options(.., holders = true)`; the Step plan, `change_refusal` ordering and the Add/Update/Replace branches are unchanged for body-less files. The `tool_import_modes` edit is only `LibraryTool { .. }` -> `LibraryTool::bare(..)` (same for `tool_library.rs`); no assertion weakened.
- Update/Replace with holders on: a changed body (or a same record with a different body, `body_same`) is a `Step::Change`, goes through `change_refusal`, which now fits the body that will stand (`landing` or the document's body) (tool_import.rs, `change_refusal`). Apply writes the body, the stamp covers it so ops go Stale; `invert` restores `(prev tool, prev body)` exactly. Pinned by `update_and_replace_take_a_changed_body_in_place_and_stale_the_op_as_set_tool_body_does`.
- Holders off in Update/Replace never clears or swaps a body (`body = None` -> Change carries no body), and the document's body must still fit the incoming record (`change_refusal` with `landing = None`), refused by name.
- File bodies are validated at parse (`read_body`: DTO re-derived + `fits`) and again at command creation (`with_options`), a bad one refuses the whole file naming the tool.
- MCP `import_tool_library` (mode + holders, typed bool check), script `cam.importTools(path, mode?, holders?)` with `cam.d.ts` and verb signature regenerated, UI checkbox with structural assertions; no snapshot PNGs or goldens touched. camcraft-mcp skill line updated, PROCESS_VERSION 18 -> 19.
- No unwrap/expect/panic outside tests; provenance lines present; changelog/Fixes present in the body; the `rotary_law_tests.rs` `neck: None` one-liner is fine.

**Local results (PR merged with current upstream/main, clean merge, built in own worktree)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| tool_library_holders | 8 passed |
| tool_library | 13 passed |
| tool_import_modes | 9 passed |

| tool_body / _bands / _judged / _view / _drill_probe | 12 / 13 / 8 / 7 / 5 passed |

| scripting | 18 passed |
| camcraft-app --lib | 138 passed |
| camcraft-ui --lib (CWD crates/ui) | 564 passed, 5 ignored |
| clippy app + ui, all targets, -D warnings | clean |

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. `PROCESS_VERSION` 19 will collide with other open process PRs; whichever merges second renumbers when it merges main. Post the #681 announcement at merge.
2. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/pages.rs` (1754 lines) and `state.rs` (4300) were already far over ~400 lines; this PR adds only a handful of lines to the former.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
